seats.oldValue: Sends the girl out for nails, then he goes after her.
seats.newValue: Goes after the girl, to tell her which size to get.
seats.execution: Gives the right errand to the wrong person. Line 9 has him send one of the boys after the girl to tell her what size to get; Uncle Podger does not go after her himself. It also skips what he does first at lines 8 and 9, sending the girl out for nails.

seats.oldValue: He drops it and the glass stays whole.
seats.newValue: He lifts the picture, drops it, and the glass is safe.
seats.execution: Line 18 has him lift up the picture and drop it, and line 19 says he would try to save the glass, and cut himself. The option turns the try into a success, so the glass is safe, and leaves out the cut. Lines 24 and 25 show the glass was not saved: a new glass had been got.

seats.oldValue: Because his tools are in the coat, and nobody knows where the coat is.
seats.newValue: Because his tools are in his coat pocket, and he has put it somewhere.
seats.execution: Lines 20 and 21 put the handkerchief in the pocket of the coat he had taken off, and lines 21 and 22 say he did not know where he had put the coat. The tools are what the house leaves off looking for at line 22; the child moves the pocket from the handkerchief to the tools.

seats.oldValue: Hide the hammer so he cannot start at all.
seats.newValue: Have him spend a week away while she does the job.
seats.execution: Lines 49 to 51 have Aunt Maria hope to be told in time, so that she can go and spend a week with her mother while the nail is hammered in. The child swaps the two people, so Uncle Podger goes away and she does the job. She never offers to do it.

seats.oldValue: A baking-tin for salt, and a glass ash-tray for bread.
seats.newValue: They light the fire, and then put the kettle on.
seats.execution: True at line 20, where they light the fire and put the kettle on before arranging the crockery for breakfast. It is what they do, not what they use for the table; lines 21 and 22 give the glass ash-tray for salt and the baking-tin for bread.

seats.oldValue: She had broken her own arm.
seats.newValue: Mrs Viney had broken her own arm.
seats.execution: Lines 54 and 55 give the broken arm to her son-in-law, not to Mrs Viney. The child keeps the right event, a broken arm, and gives it to the wrong person, the one who left the note.

seats.oldValue: The rabbits peer and the squirrels run away.
seats.newValue: The rabbits look and the squirrels dash off.
seats.execution: Swaps which animal does which. Lines 5 to 7 have the squirrels peer at them from the beech-trees and the rabbits scud away through the brushwood. This option gives the looking to the rabbits and the running to the squirrels.

seats.oldValue: Lady Canterville agreed to Mrs Otis's earnest request.
seats.newValue: Mrs Otis made an earnest request and Lady Canterville consented.
seats.execution: Lines 13 and 14 run the other way: the earnest request is Lady Canterville's, and it is Mrs Otis who consented to keep Mrs Umney in her former position. The child swaps who asked and who agreed.

seats.oldValue: Whether he will run away tomorrow; he says he will.
seats.newValue: Maggie asks whether Tom will run away; he says he will.
seats.execution: The option has Maggie ask the question of lines 7 and 8, but at lines 9 and 10 Tom answers no, and says it twice. The option keeps the content words of his answer and drops the no, so he says he will.

seats.oldValue: The pudding, which Maggie has guessed will be apricot roll-up.
seats.newValue: Apricot roll-up, which is what Maggie has guessed.
seats.execution: Swaps who knows. Maggie's guess at line 16 is the tipsy-cake, which Tom turns down; at lines 18 and 19 it is Tom who says he knows what the pudding is to be, apricot roll-up.

seats.oldValue: She gives up the best piece out of pure sacrifice.
seats.newValue: She only cares that Tom should enjoy as much puff as possible.
seats.execution: Lines 33 to 35 weigh two wants: she cared less that Tom should enjoy the utmost possible amount of puff than that he should be pleased with her. The child misses the less and the than, and the option's only makes the weaker want her whole reason. Line 35 then says so she shut her eyes, which follows from the second want.

seats.oldValue: First he uses it on Mark running ahead, but then on a made-up example.
seats.newValue: First he uses it on Mark running ahead, but then on an imaginary elephant hunt.
seats.execution: Both uses are real, in the wrong order. The imaginary elephant hunt is the made-up example at lines 10 to 17. Mark gets ahead from line 30, and Bevis turns the rule on that at lines 85 to 88. Only the order differs from the text, so retagged from en-chronology-collapse, which needs a later cause for an earlier effect.
